what: Rehearsal of round R2 with the commands of a public deployment: keys, deployment from the committed builds, verification, an operator's round over two epochs (controlled self-test, then standard) with a settled block that lags, close records, audits; then two contract accounts taking part as themselves on a deployment of their own; then ledger v2 deployed from its own builds, superseding the first deployment, and checked against its manifest

checks.check: keys are not made inside the repository's checkout
a key file is its owner's alone, and a second run keeps every key
without --yes the deployment is planned and nothing is sent
the kernel is deployed from the committed builds and read back as configured
a second deployment over an existing manifest is refused
pouw verify: the code on chain is the committed builds, wired as the manifest says
pouw verify differs (exit status 2) when the manifest records another code hash
before genesis the round does nothing and says when to come back (exit status 3)
epoch 0 (controlled self-test): a test tender in each direction is settled and confirmed, and both wallets do the audit job
run again in the same epoch, the round finds its work on chain and does nothing twice
a key that does not own a tender cannot confirm it: refused with NotDemander
a second pouw work for the same instance finds its receipt by the contribution id and sends nothing
an audit of an epoch that has not ended is refused (exit status 3)
a close record for a running epoch is refused with EpochNotEnded
a key file that others can read is refused before anything is sent
epoch 0 has ended but is not settled: an audit waits (exit status 3)
epoch 1 before epoch 0 is settled: the tenders are done, the audit jobs wait (exit status 3)
with --wait the round waits for the settled block and then does the audit jobs: each recomputes epoch 0 in full
epoch 1 (standard): the tenders between declared-related wallets are measured and not subsidized
after the round's last epoch the round writes its close record and starts no new work
epoch 0: the audit - a process with the manifest and the endpoint, no key - agrees with the ledger on every figure
epoch 0: every row of the audit's table equals the ledger's view
epoch 0: the audit read one block and names it; the epoch's close record lies within that block
epoch 0: an audit repeated at that block has the same result hash; the hashes of both records are those of their canonical form
epoch 1: the audit - a process with the manifest and the endpoint, no key - agrees with the ledger on every figure
epoch 1: every row of the audit's table equals the ledger's view
epoch 1: the audit read one block and names it; the epoch's close record lies within that block
epoch 1: an audit repeated at that block has the same result hash; the hashes of both records are those of their canonical form
epoch 0 is a controlled self-test: budget 1000 as 100 / 900, each wallet 25 + 225 test points - the capped share of either pool - and half the budget unallocated
epoch 1 is standard: each wallet 25 test points from the audit job; the tenders count 100 GMU measured and none subsidized
the audit adds the table up per declared operator: one operator, two addresses, twice the share an address can have
every record carries the deployment's labels
no contract of the kernel holds funds; the bounties were paid by the tenders' own vaults
the identity check reads that the agents are contract accounts, that the tender is the account's and that a key alone would not be accepted
pouw work --account: the worker of record is the account, driven by its key, and the admitted account is subsidized
the same key sending by itself is another worker: recorded under the key's own address, measured, not admitted, not subsidized
a key the account does not obey is refused before anything is sent
a tender owned by an account is not confirmed by the account's key sending by itself: refused with NotDemander
pouw bridge --account: confirmed by the owning account for the delivering account; declared-related, subsidized under the controlled self-test
a tender delivered before the deployment's first epoch is recorded and measured, and earns nothing
the audit of the accounts' epoch agrees with the ledger: three workers of record - two accounts and one key
v2: without --yes the deployment is planned and nothing is sent; the plan names what it supersedes and what the cell guard would answer
v2: deployed from build/v2 and read back as configured - code, wiring, log starts, the guard and its code hash, the policy
v2: the manifest names the deployment it supersedes by name, ledger and the SHA-256 of its manifest, and the guard bound to the cell
v2: a second deployment over an existing manifest is refused, and the manifest is left as it was
v2: the deployment checked from the outside against its manifest, at the finalized block

The record is evidence that the commands of a public deployment work end to end and that an independent recomputation agrees with the ledger. It is not evidence of independent participation, of demand, or of any amount of computation.

Keys, deployment, verification, rounds, audits and the identity check ran as separate processes against an endpoint, as on a public chain. The script moved the node's clock, set the stand-in for the L1Block predeploy, deployed the ERC-8414 reference contract, funded the steward, and held back the endpoint's finalized block for a while in epoch 1.
Blocks were mined every 250 ms, not one per transaction: transactions waited in the pool as they do on a public chain. Epochs are the two hours of the round's configuration, on the node's clock.

The contract accounts are the test account of contracts/testing: one owner key and an execute call. They show that the kernel and the client treat an account as the party; they are not an agent's node, and nothing here was done through one.
The test tenders settle a fixed result and carry no task.
